- No distinct concentric ring lesions, no white powder, no water-soaked lesions
- Diffuse yellowing pattern, leaf shape intact (not curled)

Top candidates: Leaf_Mold, Septoria_Leaf_Spot, Spider_Mites, Verticillium_Wilt. Let me check references.
The Leaf_Mold bottom-right panel is very similar to the test image. Let me also check viral diseases and other candidates.
Let me check remaining candidates to rule out.

- **Early_Blight**: Dark necrotic bull's-eye lesions — absent in test image ❌
- **Bacterial_Spot**: Distinct water-soaked spots → brown necrosis — absent ❌
- **Target_Spot**: Small round dark spots — absent ❌
- **Late_Blight**: Dark brown water-soaked patches, white sporulation — absent ❌
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery coating — absent ❌
- **TYLCV**: Curled/cupped leaves — test leaf is flat ❌
- **Tomato_Mosaic_Virus / Mosaic_Virus**: Subtle green mottling without distinct yellow patches — doesn't match well ❌
- **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**: Distinct small spots with dark centers — not visible ❌
- **Spider_Mites**: Bronze stippling overall — test image has distinct pale patches, not stippling ❌
- **Leaf_Mold** ✅: Pale yellowish patches on the upper leaf surface (corresponding to olive-brown mold colonies below) — the diffuse pale yellow/greenish-yellow blotchy areas on an otherwise green, flat, intact tomato leaflet matches the Leaf_Mold reference (particularly the bottom-right panel showing inter-veinal yellow patches on a green leaf)
